name: The Medinas of the Historic Sultanates of the Comoros
subtitle: A cultural property on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2026.

parts.text: UNESCO describes the property in these words: “The serial property is composed of six historic towns which developed from urban nuclei that emerged around at least the 11th century and evolved into city-states around the 14th-15th century. They eventually became the principal urban centres of the sultanates established on the islands of the archipelago of Comoros. With a common hierarchical system of social organisation, based on matrilineal and matrilocal customs, age-group systems, and patrilineal Islamic traditions still alive today, the property showcases insular urban forms and architectural expressions that resulted from cultural exchanges related to migration and Indian Ocean trade networks, embedded in the local social, geographical, and environmental context.”

Wikipedia's list of World Heritage Sites in Comoros says the country accepted the convention on 27 September 2000, and that the Medinas of the Historic Sultanates of the Comoros, its only World Heritage Site, were listed in 2026, with three more sites on the tentative list.

gaps: Almost everything beyond the listing year: which medinas, their history and what residents say about them.
